name: Follicular lymphoma
theme: the scoreboard is burden, not survival · the confirmatory-evidence ledger

meta.title: Follicular lymphoma in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults with classic FL - the most common indolent lymphoma, a decades-long disease where median survival in the modern era is NOT REACHED and where the honest scoreboard for most choices is treatment burden and time off therapy, not survival. Duodenal-type and adult pediatric-type FL stay inside this spec (indolent variants on the same pathway). Grade 3B (WHO-HAEM5: follicular large B-cell lymphoma) is managed as DLBCL and reroutes to the live DLBCL trainer, as does histologic transformation; primary cutaneous follicle centre lymphoma belongs to a different guideline and reroutes to its queued row.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease where the scoreboard is burden, not survival: every frontline strategy from watch-and-wait to obinutuzumab-chemotherapy renders the same survival number (property-enforced flatness), because that is what randomized evidence shows - the real choices are made in progression-free time, clinic visits, and toxicity. POD24 is the forecast that changes everything (5-yr OS 50% vs 90%), watch-and-wait is a ranked arm with 16-year randomized follow-up, and the relapsed screen carries the field's heaviest CONFIRMATORY-EVIDENCE LEDGER: five accelerated…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022) / ICC (2022): classic FL (grading optional in WHO-HAEM5; ICC retains 1-2/3A/3B); grade 3B renamed follicular large B-cell lymphoma; pediatric-type, duodenal-type, PCFCL, and in situ follicular neoplasm are distinct
meta.response: Lugano 2014 criteria; GELF criteria govern WHETHER to treat, which in this disease is the bigger decision

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: Median age at diagnosis is in the 60s, and the disease runs in decades - age over 60 is a FLIPI factor, but in an indolent lymphoma the plan mostly flexes on fitness, not birthdays.
Patient.helpPatient: This lymphoma is usually diagnosed after 60 and measured in decades - plans are built for the long run.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Most FL patients are well at diagnosis - a poor performance status in an indolent lymphoma is itself a reason to re-examine the biopsy question.
Patient.helpPatient: How much daily life is limited. Most people with this lymphoma feel well - the plan intends to keep it that way.

Disease.label: Histology (expert hematopathology)
Disease.help: WHO-HAEM5 renamed grade 3B 'follicular large B-cell lymphoma' and made grading optional for the rest - because 1-2 vs 3A stopped predicting outcomes under modern therapy, while 3B behaves like DLBCL…
Disease.helpPatient: A close look at the biopsy sorts this lymphoma from two look-alikes that need different plans - one of them uses the aggressive-lymphoma trainer instead.

Disease.label: Histologic transformation
Disease.help: Transformation runs ~2% per year in the rituximab era (Link 2013). Any DLBCL area in a follicular biopsy is diagnosed and treated as DLBCL - rapid nodal growth, new B symptoms, high LDH, or a discord…
Disease.helpPatient: Rarely, this slow lymphoma changes into a fast one. That possibility is why sudden changes get a new biopsy - and why that path uses the aggressive-lymphoma trainer.

Disease.label: Stage group (Lugano)
Disease.help: ~80% present advanced, and that is NOT bad news in this disease - but the limited-stage minority gets the menu's only curative-intent card (radiotherapy with a four-decade relapse-free plateau).
Disease.helpPatient: Where the lymphoma is. Unusually, the small-stage version of this disease is the one place doctors use the word cure.

Disease.label: Tumor burden (GELF criteria)
Disease.help: The disease's biggest fork: GELF-negative disease earns a real choice between observation and single-agent rituximab (both randomized-backed); GELF-positive disease earns combination therapy. The exa…
Disease.helpPatient: A checklist of size and symptoms decides whether treatment should start at all - 'not yet' is a real answer with decades of evidence behind it.

Disease.label: FLIPI risk group
Disease.help: The forecast instrument, not a treatment trigger: FLIPI drives the progression posterior; GELF drives the treat-or-observe decision. Keeping those two jobs separate is half the discipline of this dis…
Disease.helpPatient: A five-item score that says how closely to watch - it does not by itself say treatment must start.

On treatment.label: POD24 (progression within 24 months of chemoimmunotherapy)
On treatment.help: The strongest prognostic instrument this disease has is a calendar: progression within 24 months of frontline chemoimmunotherapy halves 5-year survival (50% vs 90%, FLIPI-adjusted HR 6.4). No POD24-s…
On treatment.helpPatient: If the lymphoma stays quiet for two years after treatment, the long-run outlook is excellent. An early return changes how closely the team leans in - starting with a fresh biopsy.

Relapse routing.label: Rituximab-refractory disease
Relapse routing.help: AUGMENT enrolled rituximab-SENSITIVE relapse; its OS benefit was earned there and the card honors the boundary.
Relapse routing.helpPatient: Whether the antibody that anchors most combinations still works against this lymphoma.

Relapse routing.label: Prior lines of therapy
Relapse routing.help: The 3L+ single-agent cards (CAR-T, bispecific, BTKi-combination) are labeled for two-plus prior lines; the randomized combination evidence lives at first relapse.
Relapse routing.helpPatient: How many treatments came before decides which doors are open - and there are many doors in this disease.

Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Newly diagnosed.name: Watch and wait (the strategy with 16-year randomized follow-up)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (low tumor burden, asymptomatic) - category via current version (403 this run, secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: randomized (deferred vs immediate therapy; no OS difference)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none pharmacologic; the honest cost is surveillance-anxiety, and the honest safeguard is the transformation-tempo rule
Newly diagnosed.patient: For low-burden disease without symptoms: watching closely is a real strategy - in the randomized trial with the longest follow-up in this disease, waiting cost nothing in survival, and some people never need treatment at all.

Newly diagnosed.name: Rituximab alone (RESORT: retreat as needed - same control, quarter of the doses)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (low tumor burden, therapy preferred) - category via current version (secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: infusion reactions early; years of B-cell depletion are the real ledger - infection vigilance rides along
Newly diagnosed.patient: Four antibody infusions, then treat again only if the disease stirs - the trial that tested this found it works as well as years of scheduled maintenance, with a fraction of the drug.

Newly diagnosed.name: ISRT, limited stage (the menu's one curative-intent card)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (stage I-II) - category via current version (secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: long-term retrospective series (Stanford; the curative-plateau evidence)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: site-dependent and modest at modern doses; the field is small by design
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the minority whose lymphoma is truly localized: a short course of focused radiation is the one plan in this disease where doctors use the word cure.

Newly diagnosed.name: Bendamustine + rituximab (the gentler-toxicity backbone)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (high tumor burden 1L) - category via current version (secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (StiL, BRIGHT) - PFS advantage, no OS difference
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: no alopecia, little neuropathy; prolonged T-cell suppression and the BRIGHT second-malignancy note are the fine print
Newly diagnosed.patient: The most-used combination when treatment is needed: two drugs, no hair loss, and the longest progression-free times of the classic programs.

Newly diagnosed.name: Obinutuzumab + chemotherapy (GALLIUM - PFS bought, survival unchanged)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (high tumor burden 1L) - category via current version (secondhand); FDA 1L approval 2017-11 (secondhand - confirm)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS met at 3 and 7 years; OS no difference
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: more infusion reactions, infections, and cytopenias than the rituximab arm - the price of the PFS margin, stated on the card
Newly diagnosed.patient: The newer antibody keeps the lymphoma away longer than the older one - and seven years in, survival is the same. The honest trade is more progression-free time for more side effects.

Newly diagnosed.name: Lenalidomide + rituximab, chemo-free (RELEVANCE - equivalent, never superior)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN-listed frontline option (category secondhand - confirm); FDA label covers previously-treated FL only
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - superiority NOT met; equivalence at 6 years
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: rash and cytopenias on a daily-capsule schedule; less febrile neutropenia than chemotherapy; REMS pregnancy-prevention program
Newly diagnosed.patient: A chemotherapy-free route that proved as good as - though never better than - chemotherapy: a daily capsule plus the antibody.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment in this disease still usually means years - and choosing comfort is a decision made with real numbers, not a countdown.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: R2 (AUGMENT - the confirmatory success: a PFS win that matured into OS)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (R/R, rituximab-sensitive) - category via current version (secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS primary met; OS benefit at long-term follow-up
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: cytopenias and rash on the capsule schedule; REMS program
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The relapse combination whose long game is proven: it held the lymphoma back nearly three times longer than the antibody alone - and with time, that became a survival advantage.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Tafasitamab + R2 (inMIND - the 2025 full approval)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (R/R) - category via current version (secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: adds CD19-directed infusions to the R2 ledger; cytopenias dominate
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A second antibody added to the proven relapse combination - in its trial it cut the risk of the lymphoma progressing by more than half.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Epcoritamab + R2 (EPCORE FL-1 - the bispecific that graduated)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (R/R) - category via current version (secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized combination (traditional approval 2025-11); phase 2 monotherapy numbers shown
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS mostly in step-up weeks; subcutaneous delivery; infection vigilance on the combination
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: An under-the-skin antibody that recruits your own T cells, added to the relapse combination - it recently earned the full, permanent kind of approval by beating that combination in a head-to-head trial.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: CAR-T, 3L+ (ZUMA-5 family - deep responses, approvals still provisional)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (3L+) - category via current version (secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 2 single-arm x3 (accelerated approvals; conversions pending)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS and neurologic events, front-loaded; post-REMS labels still ask for two monitored weeks nearby
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: One infusion of your own re-engineered immune cells - the deepest and longest single-treatment responses this disease has seen, with approvals that are still formally provisional while the confirming trials run.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Mosunetuzumab (off-the-shelf bispecific, fixed duration)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (3L+) - category via current version (secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 2 pivotal (accelerated approval; confirmatory readout pending)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS mostly grade 1-2 in step-up; fixed end date is the quality-of-life argument
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: An off-the-shelf antibody that recruits your T cells - no cell manufacturing wait, a planned finish line, and responses that last years in most who reach remission.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Zanubrutinib + obinutuzumab (ROSEWOOD - the chemo-free 3L doublet)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (3L+) - category via current version (secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: randomized phase 2 (accelerated approval; MAHOGANY confirmatory pending)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: BTKi ledger (bruising, atrial fibrillation vigilance) plus antibody infusion reactions
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A capsule plus an antibody - no chemotherapy, mostly outpatient rhythm, with responses in two of three people at the third line.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Tazemetostat (SADAL-era EZH2 inhibitor) - WITHDRAWN: the confirmatory trial found the harm
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NOT available as of 2026-08 (withdrawn from all markets); SYMPHONY-1 continues descriptively post-safety-measure
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 2 single-arm; accelerated approval withdrawn 2026-03 (safety, found in confirmatory trial)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: historical ledger now led by the finding that withdrew it: secondary hematologic malignancies on extended exposure
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: This drug is no longer available anywhere - the trial run to confirm its benefit instead found a serious late harm, and its maker withdrew it everywhere. The card stays visible because that safety system working is worth seeing.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: PI3K inhibitors (class of four) - WITHDRAWN: the ledger's biggest entry
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NOT available for FL as of 2026-08 (all four withdrawn in this indication)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: historical class ledger: colitis, transaminitis, pneumonitis, infections - and for umbralisib, the OS imbalance that ended it
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Four related drugs were all approved early for this lymphoma, and all four were later withdrawn - one because survival looked worse, the others because the proving trials failed or never finished. The cards stay so the pattern stays visible.
drugs: Idelalisib / duvelisib / umbralisib / copanlisib - all withdrawn in FL

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort with symptoms managed well - in this disease that chapter is usually measured in years, and the door back stays open.

milestones.title: Grade + GELF criteria + transformation vigilance
review: grade + GELF criteria decide IF treatment starts (watch-and-wait is 16-year-proven, firsthand)
POD24 is the disease's alarm: progression within 24 months of chemo-immunotherapy = 5-yr OS 50% vs 90% (HR ~6.4 firsthand) - early progressors route to the modern shelf,…
transformation vigilance at every progression (biopsy the discordant node)
EZH2 status graded the tazemetostat response; the shelf now spans fixed-duration bispecific / CAR-T-with-curative-question / oral BTK - preference axes are real

Mac Manus & Hoppe. Is radiotherapy curative for stage I-II low-grade FL? Pre-rituximab/pre-PET caveats carried on the card. JCO 1996;14:1282-90 | PMID 8648385 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

FDA safety alert: increased risk of secondary hematologic malignancies with tazemetostat (found by SYMPHONY-1 safety monitoring, >5% vs 1.7% at approval); Ipsen withdrew the drug from all markets ~2026-03; Federal Register NDA withdrawal 2026-06-22 (dates partly secondhand - confirm)
Federal Register (2022-05-26): withdrawal of idelalisib's relapsed FL (and SLL) accelerated-approval indications - the required confirmatory trial could not be completed

Federal Register (2022-04-13): withdrawal of duvelisib's relapsed/refractory FL indication (sponsor-requested; confirmatory obligation abandoned); FDA separately communicated a possible increased risk of death in the CLL population (DUO)

Bayer (2023-11-13): voluntary US withdrawal of copanlisib's relapsed FL accelerated approval after CHRONOS-4 missed its primary endpoint - the class's fourth and final FL exit

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

HBV SCREENING (the reactivation law): Hwang et al., 'Hepatitis B Virus Screening and Management for Patients With Cancer Prior to Therapy: ASCO Provisional Clinical Opinion Update' (J Clin Oncol 2020;38:3698-3715 - PMID 32716741, pubmed-eutils abstract read 2026-08-27): ALL patients anticipating systemic anticancer therapy tested with 3 tests (HBsAg, anti-HBc total Ig/IgG, anti-HBs) WITHOUT delaying therapy. Chronic HBV (HBsAg+): antiviral prophylaxis through and >=12 months after therapy. Past HBV (HBsAg-/anti-HBc+) + HIGH-RISK therapy (anti-CD20 antibodies, SCT): prophylaxis during and >=12 months after; monitoring only as an adherence-dependent alternative.
